nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does increasing the velocity at the vertical inlet affect thermal mixing?
nodes.answer: Increasing the velocity at the vertical inlet improves thermal mixing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What did Kimura et al. study in their experimental research?
nodes.answer: Kimura et al. studied the velocity and temperature variations inside tee-sections in mixing vessels, utilizing flow visualization to explain the dynamics of the merging region where two OWS interact.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How did Selvam et al. contribute to the study of thermal mixing in their research?
nodes.answer: Selvam et al. experimentally studied the effect of increasing flow temperature on T-junction flow mixture behavior, in the context of nuclear power plant engineering.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the focus of Pujowidodo et al.'s recent study?
nodes.answer: Pujowidodo et al.'s recent study focused on predicting the flow of compressible fluids in a converging diverging supersonic nozzle using a novel modified k-turbulence model.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How did Lin et al. aim to analyze heat transfer performance?
nodes.answer: Lin et al. conducted a numerical study to analyze heat transfer performance under constant one-directional and oscillatory flow conditions, examining both scenarios with and without vortex generators.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What impact did the increased cross-sectional area have according to Pujowidodo et al.?
nodes.answer: According to Pujowidodo et al., the increased cross-sectional area influenced the turbulence behavior and fluid characteristics.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What did Cloete et al. demonstrate about the effectiveness of 2D methodology?
nodes.answer: Cloete et al. demonstrated that the 2D methodology is particularly effective for predicting trends in new designs through extensive 2D and 3D CFD Eulerian multiphase simulations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How did the Seebeck coefficient change from Fe11Ti3AI6 to Fe10Cr1Ti3Al6?
nodes.answer: The Seebeck coefficient increased from +27 V/K in Fe11Ti3AI6 to +39 V/K in Fe10Cr1Ti3Al6 after doping.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What improvement in the ZT value was reported by Fukuta et al. for the Fe-V-Al alloy through a grain refinement approach?
nodes.answer: Fukuta et al. reported a high ZT value of 0.37 for the Fe-V-Al alloy using a grain refinement approach.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec technology advances_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What strategy is proposed to increase the Seebeck coefficient of the Fe11Ti3AI6 alloy?
nodes.answer: The strategy proposed is to increase the Seebeck coefficient by adding an additional transition element into the alloy, specifically by replacing Fe with Cr.
